## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | The live pages disagree. The instructions page says that once the editor has assessed suitability the paper is "single anonymous peer reviewed by two independent, anonymous expert" referees (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=rpex20&page=instructions, read 2026-11-24). The about page says: "All research articles published in this journal have undergone rigorous double anonymized peer review, based on initial editor screening and anonymized refereeing by at least two r[eferees]" (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/rpex20/about-this-journal, read 2026-11-24). The instructions warn that anonymity cannot be guaranteed for a paper already on a preprint server. The 2022 copies said double blind (aims, 2022-08-06) and "single or double blind" (instructions, 2022-06-23). Which applies in practice is not established; an author should ask the editors. Critical Notes and Discussions are also subject to a review process (live instructions). Retrieved 2026-11-24 |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No source read stating that reports are published |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev reports 2.0 review rounds and 2.0 review reports for its 1 review (https://scirev.org/journal/philosophical-explorations/). In the APA survey, 8 of 31 first verdicts were revise-and-resubmit and 11 second verdicts were acceptances (https://apasurvey.philx.org/surveys/export_csv); the survey's average number of reviewers is 2.0 (https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/export_csv) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source read |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Partly. The live instructions page (read in a real browser 2026-11-24) asks every submission to include a "Declaration of generative AI use": a statement disclosing whether and how generative AI was used in the research and manuscript preparation (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=rpex20&page=instructions). The 2022-06-23 copy predates this. The publisher-wide Taylor & Francis policy applies |

Editors and reviewers must not upload unpublished manuscripts into AI tools, and reviewers must not use AI to write review reports |
| **Source URL** | https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/ |

> Publisher-level policy, not journal-specific. Source: https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/research-impact/sharing-versions-of-journal-articles/ (retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal-specific embargo was not looked up.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|

The journal's own instructions copy (2022-06-23) adds that anonymity cannot be guaranteed for a paper already on a preprint server |
| Under review | Blank | The page speaks of the original manuscript and does not separately address the under-review stage |

| Version of Record | Eprint links and open-access sharing | Free eprint links (up to 50 uses) or eReader links; open access articles have no sharing restrictions, per the same page |

## Format

> Source for every row unless stated: the journal's live instructions for authors (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=rpex20&page=instructions), read in a real browser on 2026-11-24; the page prints no date. Retrieved 2026-11-24. The Wayback copy of 2022-06-23 is older; rows that rest only on it say so.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Two types: Research Articles, and Critical Notes and Discussions (critical notices of recent publications or discussions of recent developments in any discipline that help understand mind and action; the journal does not accept critical discussions of articles published elsewhere or of the work of its editors or associate editors). The journal does not publish book reviews; English-language manuscripts only. OpenAlex types 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 109 articles, 1 editorial, 1 book review |
| **Word limit** | Research Articles: "no more than 9,000 words, inclusive of" abstract, references and endnotes; resubmissions may exceed 9,000 by 10% to address reviewers' comments. Critical Notes and Discussions: no more than 3,000 words on the same basis (live instructions, read 2026-11-24). Older, kept as older: the 2022-06-23 copy gave 10,000 words for Research Articles. Crossref page ranges give a median article length of 17 pages (25th to 75th percentile 14 to 19) across all 111 records, 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=issn:1386-9795) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Partly. The live instructions allow resubmissions to exceed the 9,000-word limit by 10% to address reviewers' comments; no other exception is stated |
| **Abstract limit** | Unstructured abstract of 200 words; between 3 and 6 keywords (live instructions, read 2026-11-24; same for both article types) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the word limits. The instructions ask authors to avoid lengthy bibliographies |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplemental material (video, dataset, files) is published via Figshare |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit stated. Figures at 1200 dpi line art, 600 dpi greyscale, 300 dpi colour; editable tables. Colour in print is charged (GBP 300 per figure for the first four, GBP 50 from the fifth) |
| **Style / submission format** | Any spelling style if consistent; single quotation marks; Word or LaTeX (templates for both are offered); Crossref similarity screening is standard for T&F journals. The content guidance asks for articles relevant to the philosophy of mind and action, of systematic character and accessible to readers with a general philosophical background, with conceptual clarity and quality of argumentation, and without excessive jargon, elaborate cross-referencing or argumentative footnotes |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope statement is published by the journal: the aims copy (2022-08-06) says the journal aims to publish outstanding articles in the philosophy of mind and action, with an emphasis on the interrelations between cognition and agency; related disciplines are welcome "in so far as these disciplines relate to the general theme of the journal" (instructions copy 2022-06-23, https://web.archive.org/web/20220623101300/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rpex20).
- **What kind of engagement?** Articles should be relevant for the philosophy of mind and action, have a systematic character and be accessible to readers with a general philosophical background; conceptual clarity and quality of argumentation are highly valued (same copy). In the 108 abstracts, argument verbs appear in 66 (61.1%) and action, agency or intention terms in 57 (52.8%).
- **Article type and length**: Research Articles up to 10,000 words and Critical Notes and Discussions up to 3,000 words, both including abstract, references and endnotes; abstract 200 words and 3 to 6 keywords (same copy).
- **Open call seen**: none read; the special-issues page was not read (see Publication Frequency).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are OpenAlex works of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (111 records, 108 with abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex in AI-Research Notes; shares use 108 as denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 2 | "experiment-, experimental or randomised" 3 of 108 (2.8%); "quantitative, statistical or regression" 0 of 108 |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | "survey, questionnaire, interview or qualitative" 2 of 108 (1.9%) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | "autoethnograph-" 0 of 108 abstracts and 0 of 111 titles |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | argument-verb pattern 66 of 108 (61.1%); "conceptual" 4 (3.7%) |
| Mixed methods | 0 | "mixed methods" 0 of 108 |
| Meta-analysis | 0 | "systematic review or meta-analysis" 0 of 108 |
| Empirically informed philosophy (added row) | 3 | "neuroscience, psychology, cognitive science or fMRI" 16 of 108 (14.8%); "empirical" 8 (7.4%) |
| Phenomenological (added row) | 3 | "phenomenolog-" 14 of 108 (13.0%) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|

Work is mostly non-empirical by keyword count (2 of 108 abstracts mention survey, questionnaire, interview or qualitative), which is not itself an ethics rule |

| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The instructions copy asks for full name and affiliation on the cover page and states no independent-scholar rule (URL above). No board entry on the archived board page is marked as an independent scholar |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The journal applies the publisher's Basic Data Sharing Policy: sharing is encouraged, not required, where human-subject protection permits; a data availability statement is encouraged (instructions copy 2022-06-23) |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: OpenAlex counts (methods, topics, countries, types) 4 (108 of 111 records have abstracts and regexes are word-bounded and listed below, but the journal is small, so shares rest on small counts); publisher-wide policies 4; journal-specific policies and guidelines 4 (live instructions and about pages read in a real browser 2026-11-24, undated; the instructions and about pages disagree on single versus double anonymous review; the 2022 Wayback copies are kept as labelled older figures); experiential layer 2 (APA Journal Survey 31 reports, SciRev 1 review, self-reported and anonymous).

**Method note:** OpenAlex works were fetched with page-based paging (no key, no email, one request per 2 seconds; no HTTP 429 occurred). Counts are computed locally over title plus reconstructed abstract with the regexes below (case-insensitive unless a name is marked case-sensitive); word-boundary matching avoids substring inflation. Crossref lists the same 111 records but none carries an abstract, so Crossref was used only for the record count and page ranges. Counts are lower bounds for any topic expressed without the listed words; some patterns are broad (for example "action", "will", "self", "identity"). The scoring convention is stated in Methodological Preferences.

**Regexes used** (all with word boundaries): argue `I argue|we argue|this (paper|article|essay) argues?|I (defend|propose|suggest|claim|show|offer)|we (defend|propose|suggest|claim|show|offer)`; conceptual `conceptual`; empirical `empirical\w*`; experiment `experiments?|experimental|randomi[sz]ed`; neuroscience `neuroscien\w+|psycholog\w+|cognitive science|fMRI`; survey `surveys?|questionnaires?|interviews?|qualitative`; quantitative `quantitative|statistic\w*|regression`; formal `formal\w*|Bayesian|model(l)?ing|computational|predictive (processing|coding)|game[- ]theor\w*`; phenomenology `phenomenolog\w+`; review `systematic review|meta-analys\w+`; mixed `mixed[- ]methods?`; autoethnography `autoethnograph\w*`; named thinkers case-sensitive (for example `Hume\w*`, `Anscombe\w*`, `Davidson\w*`); 4E `enactiv\w+|embod\w+|4E|extended mind`; virtue `virtue\w*`; action `action\w*|agen(cy|t|ts|tial)|intention\w*|volition\w*|will`; free will `free will|responsib\w+|blame\w*|determinis\w+|compatibilis\w+|autonomy`; mind `consciousness|mental|mind|experience|phenomenal`; emotion `emotion\w*|affect\w*|feeling\w*|mood\w*|grief|shame|guilt|anger`; perception `perception|perceptual|cognition|cognitive|attention|memory`; self `self|selves|personal identity|identity`; moral `moral\w*|ethic\w*|normative|virtue\w*|welfare|well-being`; social `social|political|justice|democra\w+|collective|group`; epistemology `epistem\w+|knowledge|belief\w*|justif\w+|testimon\w+`; psychiatry `psychiatr\w+|disorder\w*|delusion\w*|addiction|depression|autism`; gender `gender\w*|feminis\w+|women|sexis\w+`; race `rac(e|ial|ism|ist)|whiteness|slavery`; decolonial `decoloni\w+|indigenous|postcolonial\w*|colonial\w*|imperial\w*`; queer `queer|trans(gender)?|LGBT\w*|sexual orientation|homosexual\w*`; religion `religio\w+|Christian\w*|Islam\w*|Buddhis\w+|theolog\w+|Jewish|Judais\w+|God`; AI `artificial intelligence|AI|ChatGPT|machine learning|large language model\w*|LLMs?`; politics `political|politics|populis\w+|democra\w+|injustice|oppress\w+`; climate `climate|environment\w*`; war `war|violence|terroris\w+`; COVID `COVID\w*|pandemic`; death etc. `death|dying|suicide|abortion|euthanasia|animals?`; first person `I|we|my|our` (case-sensitive).

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the journal's aims and instructions limit it to the philosophy of mind and action and related disciplines in so far as they relate to that theme (Framing Requirements; archived aims and instructions).
- **Length**: Research Articles up to 9,000 words (10% more allowed on resubmission) and Critical Notes and Discussions up to 3,000 words, both including abstract, references and endnotes (Format, live instructions read 2026-11-24).
- **Article type**: no book reviews, and no critical discussions of articles published elsewhere or of the work of the journal's editors (Format).
- **Language**: English only (2022-06-23 instructions copy; this sentence was not located in the live page text read on 2026-11-24).
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative-AI use or AI-altered research images breach the publisher policy (AI Policy, https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/).
- **Anonymity**: review is double blind and a preprint removes any anonymity guarantee (Peer Review; Practical Concerns).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; ethics-approval rules are not stated in the passages of the live instructions read (Practical Concerns).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher's live block gives an average of 35 days to first decision and 112 days to the first post-review decision (no period printed; older copy of 2022-06-23: 84 and 110 days), whereas the 27 timed author reports to the APA survey average 3.6 months to a response (median 3.5, range 0.2 to 13.5) and the 1 SciRev review gives 4.5 months for the first round (Review Cycle Time). The samples are small.
- **Open access cost**: green deposit of the accepted manuscript is subject to an embargo that the publisher page gives as typically 12 months (STM) and 18 months (social sciences and humanities), with each journal's own embargo on a separate list that was not looked up, so this journal's embargo is unverified (Preprint Policy); gold open access carries an APC whose amount was not obtained (Open Access).
- **Style burden**: the journal asks for systematic, accessible papers without excessive jargon, elaborate cross-referencing, lengthy bibliographies or argumentative footnotes (Format).
- **Anonymisation work**: names and affiliations go on the cover page while review is double blind (Peer Review; Format), so the author must keep identifying content out of the manuscript body.

### Best Suited For

- Argument-led papers on action, agency, the self, emotion and consciousness: "action, agency or intention" terms appear in 57 of 108 abstracts, "mind or consciousness" in 48 and "self or identity" in 42 (Orientation).
- Philosophy of psychiatry, illness and grief: 13 of 108 abstracts match psychiatry terms and 15 works carry a mental-health or grief primary topic (Sensitive Topics; Subject Density).
- Work in dialogue with cognitive science, phenomenology or embodied cognition: 16, 14 and 13 of 108 abstracts respectively (Methodological Preferences; Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Single-author papers: 93 of 109 articles (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Papers outside the philosophy of mind and action, including social or political philosophy with no link to the theme: "social or political" appears in 14 of 108 abstracts and politics terms in 5 (Orientation; Sensitive Topics).
- Primarily empirical or qualitative studies: "survey, questionnaire, interview or qualitative" appears in 2 of 108 abstracts (Methodological Preferences). This shows the form is rare here, not that it is rejected.
- Book reviews and replies to articles published elsewhere (Hard Blockers).
- Authors who need a firm anonymity model before submitting: the live instructions say single anonymous and the live about page says double anonymized (Peer Review).

| 2 | [Mind & Language](../philosophy/mind-and-language.md) | Same subject area (philosophy of mind); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | [Philosophical Studies](../philosophy/philosophical-studies.md) | General philosophy venue covering mind and action; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
